# E25 build plan

Status: planning only, awaiting independent review and the prerequisites below. No product code, tests or CI results are claimed. The design stays frozen. All citations are repository relative.

## Build order and connections

| Task | Concern | Starts after |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Validated routine release, loader checks and configuration | E01 kernel, generated contracts and configuration framework |
| T2 | Pure occurrence, cadence, hold, trigger, question and projection rules | T1 |
| T3 | Repository protocols, DTO mapping and additive SQLite persistence | T2 |
| T4 | Commands, subscriptions, deadlines, ten HTTP operations and registration | T3 |
| T5 | Routine feature UI, task entry and printed cards | E01 generated client and E03 shell interfaces; independent of T1 to T4 for component work |
| T6 | Real-stack acceptance, faults, scenario trace and measurements | T4 and T5; also the real providers used by each scenario |

T1 and T5 can start together once their external prerequisites exist. T2 supplies rules to T3 and T4. T3 never owns transactions: repositories use SYSTEM 5.7 StorageSession in the caller's UnitOfWork. T4 wires E23 mission facts, E24 warning events and E03 check events to those rules, then emits contracted routine events after atomic writes. T5 uses the generated HTTP client and E03 shell, never a second scheduler or command queue. T6 verifies the composed system rather than replacing its internals. Tasks may prepare tests against agreed ports earlier, but their dependency and acceptance gates still apply.

The snapshot has no `hub/`, `ui/`, `eval/`, hub contract copies or runtime routine documents. `contracts/` and `config/` currently contain the pharmacy artifacts. E01 supplies `crew_health.kernel.testing`, composition, generation and toolchain before dependent implementation; no task creates substitutes. SYSTEM 9 makes E01 and E23 hard dependencies. E02 authentication, E03 checks/shell, E24 rules, E05 measurement and E31 drill counterparts are required for their respective acceptance tests even where optional for running the scheduler. E21 owns the demo fixture and runner; E29 owns approved communications. See docs/SYSTEM.md:1636, docs/SYSTEM.md:2338 and docs/tdd/E25.md:1131.

Ownership was checked against every available `docs/build/*/tasks.json` and the other designs' section 13. All product paths are within E25 section 13. Test filenames in tasks.json are explicit new allocations beneath its test globs, not claims that those files already exist. No task owns shell files, contract generation, shared settings, the runner, the fixture or another epic's configuration. Recheck the inventories before dispatch because other planners are writing concurrently. Rule: an input observed earlier is not proof that it still exists; validate every required read again at dispatch. The previously read E29 design and E31 request file disappeared during planning, and E31 now exposes its older bool-only completion seam. Neither earlier proposal is treated as delivered; request their current authoritative replacements before integration. No extra package initializer, architecture manifest or replica schema is implicitly authorized.

## Design deviations

| Design / review | Winning rule | Build |
|---|---|---|
| Sections 2, 4.2, 5.3; review 18, 24 | SYSTEM 5.1 to 5.12, 6.2 to 6.5 | Use SessionContext, HubSettings.integer/quantity/boolean/text, Scheduler.replace/cancel and generation checks. There is no HubSettings.get or Scheduler.call_at. Use shared generated enums and error tables. Mission clock IDs are opaque strings; correction revisions are separate integers. Use TimeInput and ClockCorrections, not E25 time arithmetic across process epochs. |
| Sections 4.3.1, 4.6; review 1 | D13; SYSTEM 5.10.2 and 8.6 | Register EvaluatorRegistration and invoke EvaluationIsolation. Catch only EvaluatorComputationFailure for known allowlisted calculation failures. Corrupt rows, storage, I/O, integrity, authorization and validation errors abort the producer. E01 owns markers, retry identity, backoff and exhausted pending state. E25 reapply.py delegates; no routine retry queue, broad wrapper or startup retry of every parked job. |
| Sections 3.12.3, 8 test 025(c); review 14 | AGENTS 6 configuration activation; D8; SYSTEM 5.6 | Open occurrences, question instances and overrides retain their release, guidance and policy pins. Activation changes new work only; it does not move an existing preferred time. Test an existing 13:00 obligation retaining its pin and a new obligation using 14:00. Completing open work records its original guidance release. R-E25-B2 must settle how the existing item-only task endpoint serves that pin to another client. |
| DE25-15, sections 3.12.2, 3.15 INV-17, 9, 12 test 098 and 12.2; review 7 | Q1/Q7/Q18; SYSTEM 8.2 | Clinical review absence is a visible label and never a runtime gate. Source/hash/purpose, withdrawal, origin, environment, equipment and operator checks still apply in SIM as well as LIVE. No bypass when guidance is absent. `routine_task` and `operator=self` are not current shared enum values; request the former and an exact mapper to supported Requirements, never cast or relabel a task as a passage. |
| Section 3.14 and tests 027/110; review 19 | D9; SYSTEM 8.3/8.4 | Officer, acting officer, helper and ground status do not grant personal routine data. Check current object, purpose and field grants for reads, responses, replay, events and exports. An assisted observation retains subject and actor separately. No raw barrier export through the unauthenticated barriers_since signature; use an agreed approved-snapshot boundary. |
| Sections 5.1.1, 9; review 17 | SYSTEM 5.7.1/5.7.2/8.5.1; DEPLOYMENT 4.4 | Current ownership epoch alone mutates occurrences and timers. Remote capture is an immutable pending fact with the exact SYSTEM action body, not a remote row update. Validate the certificate chain, original grant, corrected observation time and window. On-time completion may reconcile a timer miss with both retained. No HLC winner for completion versus skip or rescheduling. Replica views never become write models. R-E25-B3 covers missing artifact allocation and residual conflict disposition. |
| Sections 4.1/4.2, transition command columns and manual IDs; review 16 | D6; SYSTEM 5.8/8.6 | The shared mission-life ledger is the only acceptance/deduplication authority for all three mutations. Derived IDs and historical command references remain provenance only. Compare operation, target, semantic parameters and body; reauthorize stored results. After cache expiry return the accepted_command receipt, not a reconstructed original clinical response. |
| Section 3.8.3, test 100, R-E25-25; review 8 | D1; SYSTEM 8.1 | Definition removal cannot produce a new config_changed clear or end an override. Preserve warning/effect pins. Parse historical config_changed without loosening; fresh pinned clearing evidence or authorized medical-officer disposition with reason may end the hazard. A routine end must never resolve the warning. |
| Sections 3.13, 5.3; review 18 | SYSTEM 5.2/5.3/5.10 | Day boundaries, explicit local-time slots and a person's stated later_until instant are AbsoluteDeadline. Holds, repeat offsets, every_minutes and days durations use correction-aware elapsed anchors where duration governs; the resulting displayed time alone is not the timer authority. Recompute only through shared clock/scheduler semantics. Unknown time cannot count a miss or end a tightening. Lifecycle uncertainty stays visible, never becomes invented uptime. |
| Sections 5.4, 11; review 23 | SYSTEM 5.11 and bounded StorageSession.rows | Bound every scan, instance/answer/ask history, watermark sweep, release cache and projection cache. No unbounded Sequence query or hidden len(config) bound. Register SettingSpec through module.py with finite limits and sourced deployment values. Use evaluation.* and storage.busy_timeout_ms, not duplicate routine reapply settings or busy_timeout. R-E25-B4 gates remaining bound and snapshot signatures. |
| Sections 5.1 transition actor tags, 13 import rules; review 22, 24 | SYSTEM 5.7 Actor, 5.9 audit, 6.4; DEPLOYMENT 7.4 | Shared Actor.kind uses its exact enum; scheduler/check/drill are reason/source attribution, not invented Actor kinds. Append-only forbids UPDATE and DELETE of history. Migrations expand only and software rollback keeps data and ledger. Import rules come from E01's discovery generator, with stricter rules requested through an allocated manifest. |
| Sections 12/12.2/15; review 10, 20, 25 | AGENTS 1.9, 5.7; review's acceptance requirements | No required criterion passes by xfail, skip, omitted example field, absent provider or missing test. Preserve both conflicting assertions as findings until the package owner decides. Do not change D17 or independently invent structured clinical schedules. Run hub gates with uv --project hub; scripts/validate_contracts.py currently validates the engine, so it cannot stand in for E01's hub corpus gate. |

Review source: docs/tdd/reviews/E25.astra-r1.md:1 and docs/tdd/reviews/E25.response-r1.md:1. Responses are evidence to check, not a greenlight. Findings 2/3/4/5/6/9/11/15 are implemented by the revised periodic-history, union-hold, cross-day, admissibility, frozen-audience, question-instance, inclusive miss-span and provenance rules in E25 3.4 to 3.12. Findings 12/13/20/21 remain dependent on the requests below. Findings 1/7/8/14/16/17/18/19/22/23/24 follow the deviations above. Finding 25 requires every scenario and backup below plus the novice protocol. No review finding is considered resolved merely because the response says fixed.

## End to end evidence

T6 owns HTTP and real Playwright UI tests under `eval/scenarios/e25/`, using E21's published driver; T5 owns feature component tests. Every test uses the hub HTTP API through `create_app(settings)` and real SQLite in a temporary directory, or Playwright against that running hub. Seed only through real authenticated APIs and explicit fixture adapters. No in-hub mocks, direct table seeding or replacement repositories/evaluators/visibility. Kernel fakes are for unit tests only. Use E01's documented clock/fault composition and documented external worker fakes; unresolved harness support blocks a case. Optional model, devices, camera and ground are absent in the normal acceptance profile. Positive E24/E03/E31/E29 assertions require the real counterpart. Do not declare a whole cross-epic scenario passed from its E25 subset.

| Path / scenario | What the real-stack test proves | Design tests |
|---|---|---|

Each test carries `e25` and the assigned req/val/demo/inv IDs; independent expected schedules come from package prose/vectors, not from the same configuration used as input (docs/tdd/E25.md:1024). T6 checks complete collection of every ID in E25 12.1, including 019/020/037/038/040/041/042/047/048/050. Package contradictions and absent counterparts fail acceptance. The full hub suite reruns after a bug fix. Coverage is 95% branch for domain/application, with full safety decision condition coverage, bounded complexity and independently adjudicated mutation evidence. All task gates, independent build review, CI and AI-use rows are necessary for greenlight. Local planning checks are not implementation evidence.

## Planning verification

JSON parsing, six-task dependency order, all 56 owned allocations within E25 section 13, disjointness against 16 other current plans, existing mandatory read paths and writing constraints were checked. Product gates were not run because the hub/UI/toolchain are absent. The frozen-design command `.venv/bin/python -B scripts/design_lint.py docs/tdd/E25.md --json` returned 1 with 136 errors and 34 warnings. Findings include absent canonical requests, missing template/rule-trace headings, unresolved or unrecognized seams, and acceptance-marker recognition. Coordinator: resolve actual missing contracts and have the gate owner investigate recognition defects with regression evidence. This plan neither waives those findings nor edits the frozen design.
